column2: “An Unexpected Encounter is a fun part of the evening.” Townsend had taken a liking to him and explained patiently. “After the main auction ends, they offer some unconventional lots for amusement. Usually they're little things, but occasionally a superb piece fetches an astronomical price, or you can acquire something promising very cheaply. Recently someone bought an old Renaissance painting there. The brushwork was rather immature, the condition poor, and the signature belonged to one of Leonardo da Vinci's students. Insiders considered it an entry-level piece, so the hammer price was low. But when the buyer examined it under ultraviolet light, he found another painting beneath it: a genuine da Vinci, signature and all.”
“He hit the jackpot!” Lu Mingfei said.

“Exactly. Once the top layer of paint was removed, the price increased fivefold! Oil painters in those days reused canvases, painting over old pictures, but who would have expected a student to cover up his teacher's work?”
“What incredible luck!” Lu Mingfei exclaimed.
“Your assignment today is a lot in An Unexpected Encounter. According to certain information, it's extremely important to us.” Anjou's voice sounded in his ear. “Get it, whatever the cost.”
Lu Mingfei started and came alert. Was it his turn to take the stage?

The auctioneer's assistant wheeled out a huge black hard-shell case. The auctioneer rested a white-gloved hand on the lid and smiled around the room without hurrying to open it. It was rather like an old street salesman hawking strength pills: before smashing a stone on his chest, he had to boast and build suspense.

“This is an extraordinary lot. Every auctioneer who saw it was astonished. It is exceptionally beautiful, the pinnacle of craftsmanship, but regrettably we know nothing of its provenance, not even its age, so we cannot set an appropriate opening price. With the seller's permission, this will be one of our rare zero-reserve auctions. Each increment may be as little as one dollar.” The auctioneer raised one finger. “An opportunity not to be missed. Only... one dollar!”
A stir ran through the room. This was new and had aroused everyone's curiosity. The auctioneer was pleased with the atmosphere: the first step of his sales pitch had succeeded.
He slowly lifted the lid, his voice full of mysterious temptation. “Weapons out of myth... a set of alchemical blades!”
Sharp, dark-golden light flowed through the widening gap. Lu Mingfei froze. Suddenly he felt that the object in the case was alive; he could hear familiar breathing inside.
The lid opened. Alchemical blades? The Seven Deadly Sins! It was like meeting an old acquaintance again.

Lu Mingfei had used one of them to stab the Dragon King Norton to death, yet Norton himself had forged the weapons to slaughter dragons. Lu Mingfei had lost them in the Three Gorges Reservoir and never expected to see them again.

Someone was willing to sell a treasure on the level of a divine artifact? And it had fallen to an auction with a zero opening price? It was like an emperor getting so carried away selling offices that he began auctioning his own throne! Lu Mingfei was stunned.

“Familiar, isn't it? The Seven Deadly Sins. Both your report and Nono's said you'd found the set but lost it during the ascent.” Anjou spoke with quiet admiration. “An alchemical creation beyond its age, of incalculable value!”

Lu Mingfei shivered silently. He knew its value. He had drawn only the shortest blade, yet the metal's roar had sounded like a dragon. Holding it meant holding the power over life and death. But he didn't like the set, and hadn't much regretted losing it, because of a shadow in his heart... Once these blades were grasped, killing would begin, and even the person holding them would have no choice.
Lu Mingfei had never been able to say whether the one he'd stabbed underwater was the Dragon King Norton or his friend Old Tang, who had taught him interview techniques.
Yet here it was again, like a restless ghost returning to haunt him.

“Superb workmanship, perfectly preserved, edges as sharp as new. Their forms imitate Chinese horse-chopping sabers, Tang sabers, Japanese swords, wakizashi, Damascus blades, and so on. They're housed in a single box opened by a concealed catch...” The auctioneer spoke eloquently.

Meanwhile assistants demonstrated quick cucumber slicing, cutting rolled bamboo mats, severing iron nails and metal sheets... Apparently the auction house had no way to explain the set's origins and could only demonstrate its sharpness. Lu Mingfei knew the style: Chinese TV shopping channels used the same enthusiasm to sell whitening or waist-slimming products.
“Replicas, surely? However well preserved, they couldn't be completely flawless,” someone in the VIP seats objected. “They look like Swiss Army knives made this year!”

“As I said, we can't confirm their age or provenance, so the price depends entirely on your interest. In any case they're a fine set of blades; at the very least you can use them in the kitchen.” The auctioneer shrugged and deflected the question with a joke.
“All right, one dollar!” Someone raised a paddle.
“Two dollars!” another followed immediately. The guests smiled indulgently.
“Three dollars!”
“Four dollars!”

The auctioneer looked embarrassed. The guests were teasing him. “Ladies and gentlemen, even a set of Damascus-steel kitchen knives costs hundreds of dollars. Might we have some competitive bids?” He spread his hands with a helpless smile.
“Certainly. Two hundred thousand.”

The moment the voice came from the box on the right, every eye turned toward it. Besides the startling jump in price, there was that remarkable voice: no one could explain why such a casual woman's voice should be so enchanting. Behind a deep-red velvet curtain sat a young woman in an embroidered Islamic robe, holding paddle 88. A golden veil covered her entire face; only her lovely eyes were exposed, a trace of crimson at their corners. A bright red cord tied her high-styled hair.
She sat with her eyes lowered, yet looked like a queen presiding over the gathering.
“Two hundred and five thousand.” After a few seconds, someone raised the bid.
This was no longer a joke. Someone clearly thought the set worth more.
“Two hundred and ten thousand!” Lu Mingfei raised his paddle. The principal had said they must have it, so this was unquestionably the time to act. It wasn't his money anyway.
“Three hundred thousand.” Without hesitation, the veiled young woman raised her paddle again.
What magnificent bidding! Every raise was a leap, every leap measured in hundreds of thousands of dollars. Number 88 was clearly even more determined than Lu Mingfei.
“Three hundred thousand to the lady with eighty-eight, going once!” The auctioneer happily raised his hammer.
“Three hundred and fifty thousand.” This bidder was seated among the VIPs.
“Four hundred thousand!” Someone followed. The VIP's bid had stirred the room.

“Damn, it's heating up. They're driving up the price.” Anjou's voice remained calm. “But don't hurry, and don't leave the field. Keep bidding, without making the jumps too obvious. It isn't time to exert ourselves yet.”
“Four hundred and ten thousand.” Lu Mingfei raised his paddle. Though he wasn't fond of the set, completing the assignment would excuse him from two makeup exams, so he was willing to try.
“One million.” Number 88 again.
The veiled girl's momentum was irresistible. Anjou didn't need to remind Lu Mingfei: however hard he tried, his biggest jumps were not even half hers.
“One million?” Even the auctioneer questioned the figure.
“One and a half million.” Number 88's voice was icy.
“One moment, madam. No one has bid against you since your last offer. Is your bid one million or one and a half?” the auctioneer asked carefully.
“What it was doesn't matter. Now it's one and a half million.”
The room erupted. This was madness: Number 88 was driving up the price of the blades by bidding against herself.
“One point six million.” Before the astonished murmurs had died away, a fresh price came from the VIP seats.
“Someone is paying close attention now,” Anjou murmured, raising his own paddle. “One point seven million.”
“Principal, didn't you say you weren't bidding?” Lu Mingfei was bewildered.

In the blink of an eye, one of their own had driven the price up another hundred thousand. Did these people have any idea what a hundred thousand dollars could do? In Lu Mingfei's hometown, fifty thousand would buy a small house, and the other fifty thousand could buy enough pirated game discs to fill it!

“Someone paying close attention means they've realized this might be extraordinary. They know me; with my temperament, I'd certainly try for something unusual, or I wouldn't be myself,” Anjou said quietly. “But you're still our trump card.”
“Two million.” Number 88's queenly presence surged again.
“Keep bidding,” Anjou ordered.

“Two... million and ten thousand!” Lu Mingfei gritted his teeth and raised his paddle. His smallholder instincts said a thousand-dollar raise was still a raise, so why not save money? But in this situation he felt he couldn't embarrass himself too badly.
“Two point one million.” Number 72 raised a paddle, apparently an ambusher who had kept hidden until now.

“Two point one million, the gentleman with seventy-two!” The auctioneer's face flushed with excitement. Apparently the auction house had struck lucky. They hadn't expected much from this unusual lot, yet the competition was now as fierce as for the gourd-shaped vase that had closed the main sale.
“Continue,” Anjou murmured.
“But I only have two million,” Lu Mingfei reminded him quietly.
“Don't worry. Once you've successfully bought it, the college will transfer the money. The two million was only your deposit to get a seat here.”
“Two point two million!” Lu Mingfei threw caution aside.
“Three.” Number 88 spoke lightly, not even bothering to say “million.”

The price rose back and forth, the air growing hot. Bidding gentlemen loosened their ties to breathe. Lu Mingfei gasped, the hand holding his cigar trembling slightly. He was caught in a torrent of money and couldn't stop. A few seconds after his bid of 5.2 million, someone raised it again. Hybrids truly were passionate lovers of fine craftsmanship: once their blood was hot, cost no longer mattered.
But Number 88 remained the focus. She held everyone down so firmly that, however they struggled, they seemed only to make her eventual victory more glorious.
What did it mean to be determined to win? This! It took both resources and nerve. A mongrel like Lu Mingfei could never summon the aura of a queen arriving. He felt he was losing, unable to hold on.
“Ten million.” Number 88 spoke casually, this time adding an entire digit.

Should he just give up? At worst he could work harder for the makeup exams next semester. This sort of assignment had never suited him. The principal must have read the mission report Chu Zihang had written for him and thought he'd been heroic in China. In truth his expressionless senior had protected him... while Senior was bleeding, Lu Mingfei had only been mooning over Chen Wenwen. Thoughts flashed through his mind.
“Ten million, going once, number eighty-eight.” The auctioneer's voice filled the room.

Yet he couldn't quite accept defeat. The old principal really did seem good to him, saying such poignant things, promising to give him a chance to learn. But please: a circus gorilla might sometimes appear to do addition, but it would never learn calculus, just as Lu Mingfei would never become Chu Zihang. He wrestled with himself.
“Ten million, going twice. Ladies and gentlemen, seize your last chance.”

Why didn't he dare fight? The principal had beaten his chest and promised to back him. Yet the enormous numbers seemed to crush him, leaving him breathless, hands and feet cold. He really couldn't do it... He'd tried hard to hold on until now... Perhaps he should let it go... Though he hated to lose.

“Mingfei, I believe in you. You must believe in yourself too. You are the one I chose; wherever you go, you will shine.” Anjou's voice seemed both near and far. “Giving up? You'll regret it, won't you?”
Lu Mingfei shuddered, as though an electric current had passed through him.
Yes, he hated to lose. Though he wanted desperately to give up, he couldn't suppress that little spark of unwillingness deep in his heart, a flame that not all the rain in the world could extinguish.
So he still had that inside him...
“Twenty million!” Number 17 raised his paddle.

Lu Mingfei's voice filled the hall, and everyone fell silent. Could it get any crazier? This young, nouveau-riche-looking big kid still trembled slightly as he raised his paddle, yet he had jumped ten million!

The auctioneer hesitated; it was the second time that day he'd wondered whether he'd heard correctly. An assistant hurried onstage and whispered to him. The auctioneer nodded slightly, his face grave. “Ladies and gentlemen, thank you for your interest in this lot. The intensity of the bidding has greatly exceeded our expectations. We must prevent false bids that result in a successful sale without payment, so we must ask Mr. Lu, number seventeen, to accompany us to the finance office. The auction will be suspended in the meantime.”
Lu Mingfei's face changed at once.
In the finance office the auctioneer's assistant and the finance manager gathered around Lu Mingfei. They were perfectly courteous, but to him they seemed full of murderous intent.

“We're very sorry, but the manner of your bidding was truly extraordinary. To safeguard the auction, we had to ask you here.” The manager patted a black briefcase. “You gave us only a Zurich bank account containing two million dollars as a deposit. Ordinarily that would be persuasive, but your bid this round is twenty million, ten times your deposit. This is your first visit, and you haven't established sufficient credit. Unless you can demonstrate that you really can pay, we must revoke your bidding privileges.”
“How could that be? Is that all?” Sweat poured down Lu Mingfei's face, but he forced himself to bluster. “Two million is just what I spend on a new Bugatti!”

The manager seemed to see through the boy's bravado and smiled discreetly. “Please cooperate and temporarily remove your earpiece and microphone. Your financial security and our reputation are at stake, so our conversation must remain confidential.”
Lu Mingfei had no choice but to remove them. Now he was fighting alone.

“In the past, malicious clients have placed newcomers in the room to drive up prices. They had no ability to pay, but affected the fairness of the auction.” The manager spoke patiently. “You only need to demonstrate your ability to pay, for example by providing us with another account.”
“Two million is only my account balance.” Lu Mingfei did his best to avoid the man's gaze.
The manager smiled and opened the briefcase. Unfolded, it became an electronic device with a red LCD screen and black keyboard, like an enormous calculator.
“Please enter the password for your Zurich bank account.” He pushed the case toward Lu Mingfei.

Lu Mingfei couldn't refuse. With stiff fingers he pressed the keys; Anjou had given him the password. A few seconds later the screen displayed “$2,000,000.00.” He stared blankly at the number that had once seemed a vast fortune, but heard quiet, derisive laughter. At this feast of dragons, the sum was insignificant.
“We have considerable access at the Zurich bank and can check your balance. It really is only two million dollars.” The manager smiled.

Laugh, laugh. These people had been laughing at him ever since he got out of the car, until he no longer knew what to do with his hands and feet. Lu Mingfei lowered his head like a suspect being questioned.
In the opera-house hall, guests murmured to one another, voices rising and falling.
Someone cleared her throat in the box on the right. Even that sound was seductive, and everyone looked up together.
“When the auction resumes, my next bid will be fifty million.” Every word from Number 88 was as heavy as a gold bar.

The auctioneer was dumbfounded. Was this a declaration of war? Was the veiled girl's fighting spirit so fierce she wouldn't even wait for the auction to resume before bidding? She was no longer a queen; she was an army at the gates!
“Number eighty-eight says she'll raise it to fifty million!” Another assistant hurried into the finance office and whispered to the manager.
“Did you hear right? Fifty million?” The manager stared, lowering his own voice. “There's nobody left bidding against her!”
“Who says there isn't?” Lu Mingfei slowly raised his head.
The manager frowned. “Sir, unless you can provide a new account with funds to prove yourself...”
Lu Mingfei looked at the balding man. Did hybrids go bald too? He looked like a washed-up middle-aged loser. A man who admitted defeat... would become a useless middle-aged uncle like that!
That little fire in his heart was so annoying... burning slowly.

“I really hate the way you look at me. It's like my high-school teacher reading my grades aloud to the whole class,” Lu Mingfei said. “And I hate the way you all laugh. Let me enter the password again.”

The strange characters shone in his mind. “Show me the money”: that cheat code would bring him ten thousand dollars, but he needed more, far more. He had no way out. If he retreated, he'd lose, and he couldn't bear it. As if possessed, he added “×10000” after the code. Ten thousand times: he would borrow a hundred million!

He tapped the confirmation key and pushed the remote device connected directly to the Zurich bank back to the manager. Crossing his legs, he smoked the Cohiba cigar, which had looked like a ridiculous grilled sausage between his fingers moments ago.
“What?” The manager smiled. “Still two million...”

He stopped suddenly, the tail of his words twisting. The number had begun to change, leaping rapidly like ultraviolet readings from the sky during a solar flare. Every digit rolled—no, flashed! Had the device used old-fashioned numerical wheels instead of an LCD, their furious rotation would have thrown sparks.
The manager involuntarily reached out to slap the device. Either it had gone mad or his eyes were wrong. A vast flood of money was pouring into this unknown boy's account.
At last the number settled at “$10,200,000.00.” In ten seconds, a hundred million dollars had poured into the account!
Lu Mingfei tilted his head back and drew a deep breath, as though he would take all the air in the world into his lungs. Then he exhaled softly. “One hundred million.”
“Yes... your account... has increased by a hundred million.” The manager stammered.

“I can see that. What I mean is, when the auction resumes, I'll bid a hundred million dollars. I like to show my hand,” Lu Mingfei said evenly. “Competitive bidding is too tedious; it wastes everyone's time. I think this set is worth a hundred million, so that's what I'll offer. There's no need to economize on something I want. If anyone bids higher, I'll let it go.”

“All right, I'm going to the restroom. Take care of this. You have my authorization; this paddle is now worth a hundred million.” Lu Mingfei tossed number 17 in front of the manager, stood, and went out.

The auctioneer was back onstage, his voice trembling, eyes bright. “The auction is now resumed. We have received authorization from the lady with number eighty-eight to bid fifty million, and authorization from Mr. Lu, number seventeen, to bid... one hundred million.”

Silence filled the hall. Everyone watched the box on the right, waiting for Number 88. The price had become utterly insane; nobody else wanted to join this contest between madmen. Whether Number 88 would fight back was the only uncertainty.
“One hundred million dollars, going once.” The auctioneer raised his hammer.
“One hundred million dollars, going twice...”
The veiled girl stood, turned without a word, and left. Suddenly she discarded the set as though it were worthless.
“Sold for one hundred million dollars!” As she walked out of the hall, the auctioneer brought down the hammer as if driving a nail hard into wood.

In the lounge outside the opera-house hall, Lu Mingfei paced in circles, thinking. The once-magnificent cigar had become a grilled sausage again between his limp fingers, seemingly a little wilted itself.

He tried to recall what had happened. For an instant an exhilarating force had surged through him, like a martial-arts master unleashing power from his dantian, or someone who had just eaten a bowl of hot, spicy tofu pudding. He had stopped caring about anything, overflowing with heroic passion and grand words. As he tossed out the paddle and that hundred million, he had been full of thoughts like, What's a hundred million to a magnificent fellow like me? I'm the man who will shatter heaven! Like a Hong Kong comic hero bursting with power and shouting, “You useless fool, don't think your Hell King's World-Splitting Fist lets you rule the world! Dare you face my hundred-thousand-horsepower Star-Shattering Divine Sword?”
Only when he happily relieved himself in the restroom did that domineering spirit flow away with his urine. He suddenly came to his senses, and his entire body went cold.
A hundred million... Holy crap, he'd actually spent a hundred million without the principal's authorization. He had thrown away a hundred million for something as insubstantial as a surge of bravado?
Had he gone mad, or just awakened from a dream? His memory tangled for a moment as he stood blankly before the urinal.
“Hey, friend, you're already finished...” a man beside him reminded him kindly.
“Can't I savor the moment?” Lu Mingfei snapped.

But after leaving the restroom he didn't dare enter the hall. He only hoped everything had been an illusion, that nothing had happened, that he hadn't spent a hundred million, that he had merely stepped out to use the restroom and after a short rest everything would return to normal.
High heels clicked crisply against the floor.
“Mr. Lu,” someone said behind him.

He spun around. The veiled Number 88 stood only a foot behind him, her eyes cold, the alluring crimson at their corners touched with menace. Lu Mingfei hopped back, nearly blurting, Let's talk this out! I didn't mean to make trouble; gentlemen use words, not fists! Her fierce aura always made him feel she might draw an Arabian scimitar from beneath her robe at any moment.
“A fine display of nerve with that final bid. I liked the blades too, but I don't have Mr. Lu's resources, so I had to let them go.” The girl actually smiled.
She leaned forward slightly and did something wonderful beyond Lu Mingfei's imagining: she kissed him lightly on the cheek! A girl's warm body heat and faint floral fragrance enveloped him.

Huh? Was this the first time a girl had kissed him? What unscrupulous person had stolen his first kiss like that? Did she have no conscience or morals? If she was going to kiss him, why not on the mouth? Why not warn him so he could prepare? If possible, he'd really hoped to make the first move himself... Countless voices echoed in his head. The whole world blurred before his eyes. Were shining red hearts rising above his head?
“You're handsome, young man... Hear the applause? They're applauding you. Perhaps one day... the whole world will applaud you.” The girl brushed past the motionless Lu Mingfei.
Applause poured from the opera-house hall like a surging tide.
A Bordeaux-red Cadillac DTS waited at the opera house's rear entrance, a Japanese flag mounted on its side. The veiled girl went straight to it and sped away.
“Wait, madam! Please wait!” The auctioneer's assistant rushed out of the opera house, only to see the DTS disappearing into the distance.
“Why didn't you stop her? Didn't I call you?” The assistant turned on the silent attendant, furious.

“It's a Japanese embassy car. Under diplomatic custom, even an embassy car flies the flag only when the ambassador or consul is aboard or when on official business,” the attendant said quietly. “She has powerful backing. It wouldn't be easy to stop her.”
The assistant paused and nodded slightly. “She's a new face. Did you check who sponsored her?”
“The Mint Club. We couldn't find anything more.”
“More and more new faces, and they're playing more and more extravagantly.” The assistant murmured, “It's unsettling...”

A partition separated the DTS's front and rear seats, and black privacy glass shut out outside eyes. On the broad sofa seat, the veiled girl curled into a ball and wriggled out of the spacious robe like a rabbit. All her bones seemed soft, every joint able to turn like a universal coupling. Only a rigorously trained yoga practitioner, contortionist, or... Japanese ninja could do that. She stretched her figure with pride. Hiding something so good beneath an Arabian robe was depressing.

The clothes she liked had been prepared: black leather top and pants, a wine-red short jacket, and red lace-up sandals with three-inch heels. Even with help, such an extremely fashionable outfit would take several minutes to put on, but for a ninja it was as easy as a hermit crab slipping into a shell. Mai Sakatoku removed the golden veil, revealing a breathtakingly beautiful face, the bright blush lending her a touch of ferocity.

A woman who always carried two ninja swords in her bag could never look harmless, however she wore her makeup. Her striking figure was even more conspicuous than her face, so she had to wrap herself from head to toe in a robe.
“As you said, a hundred million.” Reclining in the seat, she crossed her long legs and connected the car phone.

“Beautifully done. I can already see a hundred million dollars added to the account. Subtracting the salvage expenses, our net profit is ninety-eight point six million. Cassell College is rich; they only need a few dozen seconds to move that much cash.” Chips could be heard crunching on the other end.
“Their Board of Trustees is richer. Those people control trusts and syndicates; even a billion is no problem. Aren't you worried about getting fat, eating chips all the time?”
“I don't have your figure, so I won't be so demanding. As long as Levi's doesn't suggest the loose fit when I try on jeans, I'm happy.” Chips Girl was as carefree as ever.

“A woman worth that much still wears Levi's... Why pretend to be the girl next door?” Mai Sakatoku muttered. She frequented luxury boutiques, happily dividing her time off between shopping, parties, and ninja training that involved hanging from a roof by two fingers...
“Miss High-and-Mighty, without all my hard work, how would you lot live so well?”

“Tell me, wasn't a hundred million too cheap for the Seven Deadly Sins? A treasure forged by the King of Bronze and Fire himself, deadly blades capable of killing the other Dragon Kings. There'll never be another set in the world.”

“Can't be helped. The strongest weapons need the strongest wielder; they're no use to us. Would you risk being consumed by them? When their ‘Crime and Punishment’ domain expands to its limit, people of our bloodline can't even touch the hilts, can we? Actually, as long as they return to Lu Mingfei's hands, I'd gladly give them away, never mind paying the one-point-four-million salvage fee ourselves! But a gift would make Anjou suspicious, so we charged him a hundred million to help with household expenses... The economy's bad lately...” Chips Girl began rambling.
“You sound like a bookkeeper! No, a maid who keeps the accounts.”

“What do you think my role is? I'm an accounting maid!” Chips Girl sounded aggrieved. “Besides me, who among you can be relied on? Managing this whole operation isn't easy. Thousands of mouths to feed! You and that cold-faced girl know nothing about saving. Every mission you're like vandals, sweeping through and wrecking everything. The compensation bills afterward are terrifying...”
“Shut up, shut up!” Mai dreaded this routine more than anything. “Has the boss contacted you lately?”
“Once.”
“What about?” Mai grew serious.

Her boss was elusive. Usually the woman who always had chips in her mouth managed the organization's affairs single-handedly; only on matters of exceptional importance did the boss give orders personally, and every time the move was fierce, overwhelming, and violent.
“Do you know a company called Square Enix?”

“Obviously. Square, Japan's most famous game-software company, known for Final Fantasy. It's practically the national company of Japanese gaming obsessives, and I'm Japanese.” Mai was a loyal Square player herself, fond of the Valkyrie Profile series, and had completed every installment with every item.

“They recently released their newest title, Final Fantasy XIV, but the reviews were terrible. Longtime players reacted strongly. One posted passionately on the official forum: ‘Final Fantasy XIV no longer appeals to me at all. The people making games have lost their way, so there's no reason for me to keep my eighty-five million dollars in Square Enix stock. I've decided to sell.’ Just as everyone was laughing and assuming it was a joke, news came that the share price had instantly fallen 0.15 percent,” Chips Girl said lazily.
“Hey, your train of thought has wandered way too far. Is this what you Chinese call a ‘god-tier plot twist’?”
“I posted it using the boss's ID, then sold all eighty-five million dollars of his Square Enix shares on the Tokyo Stock Exchange within fifteen seconds.” The other woman hung up.
Mai stared at the receiver's busy signal... It sounded like something out of a fantasy, but it was certainly the boss's style—that supremely powerful, supremely violent... gaming nerd.
